How should I read the curves?

Every line uses the same scoring-specific trade-value scale. Player rank runs left to right; trade value runs bottom to top. Starter, bench, and waiver lines are vertical rank boundaries under every lock. No median, average, or blended composite curve is plotted.

Solid lines are as-published values reindexed to the shared scale plus ESPN’s projection-derived series. Dashed adjusted lines shift the weighting to our view of value. Missing values break that source’s line rather than becoming zero.

Notes & source definitions
  1. Scale and missing values. Values measure value above waivers on a shared scale whose true top is 87 in Standard, 86 in Half PPR, and 84 in Full PPR. Missing or unpriced values remain blank and are never converted to zero.
  2. Series taxonomy. As-published values are reindexed only onto the common scoring-specific scale. FC Adjusted, USAT Adjusted, FP Adjusted, and CBS Adjusted are adjusted best-estimate values that shift the weighting to our view of value; missing adjusted values stay blank.
  3. Sources. USA Today is an editorial chart; FantasyCalc reflects completed fantasy trades; FantasyPros is an analyst-consensus chart; CBS is an editorial chart; ESPN uses its season projections translated to the same scale.
  4. Freshness. Content date is when a source's published numbers last changed; fit date identifies the bias-adjustment bake. Week-specific references disable after the weekend rollover until the next week's artifact is present. ESPN remains live.
